sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: When designing a commercial structure, the architect must make the hallways wide enough for a wheelchair.
sentences.zh: 在设计商业建筑时，建筑师必须确保走廊足够宽，以便轮椅通过。

sentences.en: The materials must be compatible with its surrounding climate.
sentences.zh: 材料必须与其周围的气候相适应。

sentences.en: The beams must be able to support the building and withstand the wind.
sentences.zh: 梁柱必须能够支撑建筑物并经受住风力的考验。

sentences.en: The building should be dynamic, interesting, comfortable, and ready to be completely abandoned if it burns.
sentences.zh: 建筑物应该是动态的、有趣的、舒适的，并且如果发生火灾，也要做好完全废弃的准备。

sentences.en: There are a number of considerations for how a building should respond to emergency.
sentences.zh: 对于建筑物应如何应对紧急情况，有许多考量因素。

sentences.en: Horns versus strobes versus speakers.
sentences.zh: 警报器与频闪灯与扬声器的对比。

sentences.en: The pulsating frequency of the light, the intensity of the light.
sentences.zh: 灯光的脉冲频率，灯光的强度。

sentences.en: Smoke dampening, it goes on and on.
sentences.zh: 烟雾阻尼，诸如此类不一而足。

sentences.en: There's the sprinklers, the panic bars, you know, the spring-loaded horizontal bar that you push to unlock an emergency exit.
sentences.zh: 还有喷淋系统、防恐慌推杆，你知道的，就是你推一下就能打开紧急出口的弹簧加载水平杆。

sentences.en: The smoke detectors, what kinds you use, and the distances between them.
sentences.zh: 烟雾探测器，你使用哪种类型，以及它们之间的距离。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people hardly even look up and see these things, and they just need to be there when an emergency happens.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人甚至都不会抬头看一眼这些东西，它们只需要在紧急情况发生时派上用场就行。

sentences.en: Now, Adam Weinig and Daniel Scoville are architects.
sentences.zh: 现在，亚当·韦尼格和丹尼尔·斯考维尔是建筑师。

sentences.en: We work with them at ArcSign in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的 ArcSign 与他们共事。

sentences.en: Most of the time, when they're working on fire safety, they'll consult experts about where to place what kinds of architectural emergency devices.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，当他们从事消防安全工作时，他们会就各种建筑应急设备的摆放位置咨询专家。

sentences.en: But there's one safety device that they must design right into the building from the get-go.
sentences.zh: 但有一种安全设备是他们从一开始就必须直接设计到建筑中的。

sentences.en: It's impossible to ignore.
sentences.zh: 这是无法忽视的。

sentences.en: As far as stair locations, that's pretty important right from the start, because it changes the whole dynamic of your space.
sentences.zh: 就楼梯的位置而言，从一开始这就非常重要，因为它改变了你整个空间的动态。

sentences.en: Typically, buildings require two fire stairs, but it all depends on the size and purpose of the structure.
sentences.zh: 通常，建筑物需要两个消防楼梯，但这完全取决于建筑物的规模和用途。

sentences.en: In architecture and building codes, you always need a certain number of exits or means of egress, so it weighs out of a building.
sentences.zh: 在建筑和建筑规范中，你总是需要一定数量的出口或疏散通道，因此它在建筑中占据一定分量。

sentences.en: And this fire escape, precariously bolted to the side of the building, is one of our means of egress out of this space.
sentences.zh: 而这个摇摇欲坠地用螺栓固定在建筑侧面的防火梯，就是我们逃离这个空间的疏散通道之一。

sentences.en: And this is how 99% invisible is going to escape a burning building.
sentences.zh: 这就是“百分之九十九隐形”将如何逃离着火建筑的方式。

sentences.en: This is how ArcSign and 99% invisible are going to escape our burning building.
sentences.zh: 这就是 ArcSign 和“百分之九十九隐形”将如何逃离我们着火的建筑的方式。

sentences.en: In case of fire, architects Daniel Scoville and Adam Wynick and producer Avery Truffelman would put their steely resolve and athletic prowess to the teSt.
sentences.zh: 万一发生火灾，建筑师丹尼尔·斯考维尔、亚当·维尼克和制片人埃弗里·特鲁夫曼将对其坚定的决心和运动能力进行考验。

sentences.en: There's this classic wrought iron fire escape right outside of our window.
sentences.zh: 就在我们窗户外面，有一个经典的熟铁防火梯。

sentences.en: And I thought it was defunct.
sentences.zh: 我曾以为它已经废弃了。

sentences.en: It's all rusty and stuff.
sentences.zh: 它到处都是铁锈之类的东西。

sentences.en: But then, I bothered to read the sign with the evacuation plan for our building.
sentences.zh: 但后来，我费心去读了我们大楼疏散计划的标牌。

sentences.en: Always read the evacuation plan.
sentences.zh: 一定要阅读疏散计划。

sentences.en: Fire escapes are not allowed in new construction.
sentences.zh: 新建筑不允许安装防火梯。

sentences.en: But because we are in a beautiful old brick building, the fire escape is actually one of our means of egress.
sentences.zh: 但因为我们在一栋美丽的古老砖砌建筑里，所以防火梯实际上是我们的疏散通道之一。

sentences.en: We just speak of means of egress thinking of the whole route, the corridor and the stairs.
sentences.zh: 我们所说的疏散通道是指整个路线，包括走廊和楼梯。

sentences.en: And you think of an exit as being essentially the door.
sentences.zh: 你会认为出口本质上就是那扇门。

sentences.en: Professor Sarah Wormiel, independent scholar and researcher at MIT.
sentences.zh: 萨拉·沃尔米尔教授，麻省理工学院的独立学者和研究员。

sentences.en: One of my books is called The Fireproof Building.
sentences.zh: 我的一本书名叫《防火建筑》。

sentences.en: And I can't remember the subtitle.
sentences.zh: 我记不清副标题是什么了。

sentences.en: It's The Fireproof Building, Technology and Public Safety in the 19th Century American City.
sentences.zh: 它是《防火建筑：19世纪美国城市的科技与公共安全》。

sentences.en: The single most dangerous thing for architecture, historically, is fire.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，对建筑最具破坏性的单一致命因素就是火灾。

sentences.en: And in the 1700s, if a fire did break out, there wasn't a whole lot you could do about it.
sentences.zh: 在18世纪，如果真的爆发火灾，你其实无能为力。

sentences.en: By that time, there were firefighters.
sentences.zh: 到了那个时候，已经有了消防员。

sentences.en: Whom you summoned by yelling loudly.
sentences.zh: 你通过大声呼喊来召唤他们。

sentences.en: And they would come, and they would bring you the fire escape.
sentences.zh: 他们会赶来，并带给你消防逃生工具。

sentences.en: It was a cart with a ladder on it.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆载有梯子的手推车。

sentences.en: That was actually what the earliest fire escapes were.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是最早的防火梯。

sentences.en: So fire escape methods started to get incorporated into architecture, starting with the scuttle.
sentences.zh: 因此，防火逃生方法开始融入建筑中，首先出现的是天窗出口。

sentences.en: It looked like a skylight.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像一个天窗。

sentences.en: It would have some kind of cover.
sentences.zh: 它会有某种盖子。

sentences.en: It was like a trap door on the roof.
sentences.zh: 就像屋顶上的一扇活动门。

sentences.en: And then there'd be a ladder to get up and out.
sentences.zh: 然后会有一个梯子供人上去并离开。

sentences.en: And so, in a fire, you would climb through the scuttle, out onto the roof, hop to your neighbor's scuttle, and crawl into their building, which presumably hadn't also caught fire.
sentences.zh: 因此，在发生火灾时，你会爬过天窗出口，来到屋顶上，跳到你邻居的天窗出口，然后爬进他们的建筑，据推测那栋建筑当时还没有着火。

sentences.en: That was the beginning, this idea that a city could require something for the sake of fire safety.
sentences.zh: 这就是开端，即城市可以为了消防安全而强制要求某些设施的理念。

sentences.en: Around 1860, New York begins to require means of egress in tenement buildings.
sentences.zh: 大约1860年，纽约开始在公寓楼中强制要求设置疏散通道。

sentences.en: Tenement buildings were tall, flammable, densely packed tinderboxes, just full of families.
sentences.zh: 公寓楼高大、易燃、密集且像个火药桶，里面挤满了家庭。

sentences.en: So, of course, landlords went with the least expensive options.
sentences.zh: 因此，房东们自然选择了成本最低的方案。

sentences.en: The popular cheap fix was rope.
sentences.zh: 当时流行的廉价解决方法是绳索。

sentences.en: Ropes with baskets that you're supposed to somehow, you know, the building's on fire.
sentences.zh: 带有篮子的绳索，你必须以某种方式，你知道的，大楼着火了。

sentences.en: You have your kid, you're terrified, and you calmly, you know, open this little nightstand, pull out the basket with the ropes, you know, set up the apparatus, strap yourself in,
sentences.zh: 你带着孩子，吓得要命，然后你很镇定地，你知道的，打开这个小床头柜，拉出装有绳索的篮子，你知道的，架设好装置，把自己绑在里面，

sentences.en: and somehow, you know, lower yourself calmly to the ground.
sentences.zh: 然后不知怎么的，你知道的，平静地把自己放低到地面。

sentences.en: You know, it's just preposterous.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这简直荒谬至极。

sentences.en: There are these hilarious old advertisements for fake cabinets and hollow refrigerators and empty washing machines so that you can store your ropes and basket apparatus.
sentences.zh: 有一些极其搞笑的旧广告，宣传假橱柜、中空冰箱和空洗衣机，这样你就可以把绳索和篮子装置藏在里面。

sentences.en: Because no one would notice that extra washing machine.
sentences.zh: 因为没有人会注意到那台多出来的洗衣机。

sentences.en: One engineer actually thought that instead of dispatching ropes from inside, archers could shoot the ropes up to the higher floors.
sentences.zh: 曾有一位工程师认为，与其从内部投放绳索，不如由弓箭手将绳索射向高层。

sentences.en: You know, people aren't that athletic necessarily to begin with, but second of all, it's a fire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们本来就不一定那么擅长运动，其次，这是火灾。

sentences.en: You know, this isn't the best time to, you know, like, figure out how to lower yourself on a rope.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在可不是什么好时机去琢磨怎么用绳子把自己放下去。

sentences.en: Another patent proposed individual parachute hats with accompanying rubber shoes to break the fall.
sentences.zh: 另一个专利提议是配备减震降落伞帽和相应的橡胶鞋来化解坠落冲击。

sentences.en: There were also these big slide fire escapes that were largely marketed to schools as both emergency devices and playground equipment.
sentences.zh: 当时还有这些大型滑梯式防火梯，主要作为应急装置和游乐场设备向学校推销。

sentences.en: There actually used to be a giant spiral slide to escape the Claremont Hotel right here in Oakland, which would have made that place a whole lot better.
sentences.zh: 这里奥克兰的克莱蒙特酒店过去实际上有一个巨大的螺旋滑梯用于逃生，这会让那个地方好得多。

sentences.en: There were lots of ideas, but by the 1870s, fire escapes begin becoming something iron, something fixed to the building.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多想法，但到了19世纪70年代，防火梯开始变成铁质的、固定在建筑上的东西。

sentences.en: Although by that point, they still weren't anything great.
sentences.zh: 尽管到那个时候，它们仍然算不上多好。

sentences.en: They were like an iron platform outside of a window with straight ladders attached, or it might just be a straight ladder clamped to the wall.
sentences.zh: 它们就像窗户外面的一块铁平台，连着直梯，或者可能只是一个夹在墙上的直梯。

sentences.en: In some cities, the external ladders angled and widened to become more like stairs.
sentences.zh: 在某些城市，外挂梯子会倾斜并加宽，变得更像是楼梯。

sentences.en: This was an improvement, of course, but ultimately fire escapes just didn't suffice.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一个改进，但归根结底，防火梯还是不够用。

sentences.en: And it took a terrible tragedy to show this.
sentences.zh: 而这需要一场可怕的悲剧来证明这一点。

sentences.en: So the Ash Building in New York was built as a loft building, and its owners represented it as being, you know, maybe for warehousing, not necessarily for manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 因此，纽约的阿什大楼最初是作为loft建筑建造的，其业主声称它可能是用于仓储，不一定用于制造。

sentences.en: Based on its dimensions, the Ash Building was required to have three means of egress.
sentences.zh: 根据其尺寸，阿什大楼被要求必须有三个疏散通道。

sentences.en: But the developer insisted that the property would just be used as warehousing.
sentences.zh: 但开发商坚称该物业只会用作仓储。

sentences.en: So rather than three stairs, he was allowed to put in two stairs and a thin fire escape.
sentences.zh: 因此，他没有建三个楼梯，而是被允许建造两个楼梯和一个狭窄的防火梯。

sentences.en: Then the owner rents the top three floors of the Ash Building to the Triangle Shirtwaist Company.
sentences.zh: 随后，业主将阿什大楼的顶层三层租给了三角衬衫腰带公司。

sentences.en: In March of 1911, there's a fire in the buildings.
sentences.zh: 1911年3月，大楼发生了一场火灾。

sentences.en: It's not knowing exactly how it begins, and it spreads quickly.
sentences.zh: 火灾是如何开始的尚不完全清楚，并且蔓延得非常快。

sentences.en: The 10th floor has an exit to the roof, so many of the 10th floor workers are able to survive by taking the stairs up.
sentences.zh: 十楼有一个通往屋顶的出口，因此许多十楼的工人们通过往上走楼梯得以幸存。

sentences.en: And the workers on the 8th floor are, by and large, able to get out.
sentences.zh: 八楼的工人大体上也得以逃生。

sentences.en: But workers on the 9th floor were trapped.
sentences.zh: 但九楼的工人被困住了。

sentences.en: The doors to the stairs opened inward and became blocked with bodies.
sentences.zh: 通往楼梯的门是向内开的，结果被尸体堵住了。

sentences.en: And the stairs were backed up with workers exiting from the floors below, so workers on the 9th floor couldn't even get down.
sentences.zh: 而且楼梯里挤满了从下面楼层撤离的工人，所以九楼的工人根本无法下楼。

sentences.en: Only a few workers on this floor knew about the 10th floor exit, and so they didn't even try to go upstairs.
sentences.zh: 这层楼只有少数工人知道十楼的出口，因此他们甚至没有尝试往楼上走。

sentences.en: There was a charge that one of the doors was locked.
sentences.zh: 有指控称其中一扇门被锁上了。

sentences.en: And this wasn't proved at the trial, but I believe even if it had been, with all the people exiting from the 8th floor and the staircases were very narrow and winding,
sentences.zh: 这在审判中并未得到证实，但我相信即使证实了，由于八楼有所有人都在撤离，且楼梯非常狭窄且呈螺旋状，

sentences.en: there just wasn't the capacity.
sentences.zh: 容量根本不够。

sentences.en: Some workers tried to use the outside fire escape, and it collapsed under the weight.
sentences.zh: 一些工人试图使用外侧防火梯，结果它在重量下坍塌了。

sentences.en: It was from the windows of the 9th floor that many workers, desperate to escape the flames and smoke, fell or jumped to their deaths.
sentences.zh: 许多急于逃离火焰和浓烟的工人，正是从九楼的窗户坠落或跳楼身亡的。

sentences.en: 146 people lost their lives, right in the middle of Greenwich Village.
sentences.zh: 146条生命消逝了，就发生在格林威治村的正中心。

sentences.en: There were a lot of witnesses.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多目击者。

sentences.en: It was horrible.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: But the building was fine.
sentences.zh: 但建筑本身很好。

sentences.en: The Ash Building was a fireproof building.
sentences.zh: 阿什大楼是一栋防火建筑。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's still standing.
sentences.zh: 当然，它现在依然耸立着。

sentences.en: And it's now part of New York University.
sentences.zh: 它现在是纽约大学的一部分。

sentences.en: The Ash Building, now called the Brown Building, was well made.
sentences.zh: 阿什大楼现在被称为布朗大楼，它建造得很坚固。

sentences.en: Which is why, at the time, no one really thought it needed egress.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在当时，没有人真正认为它需要疏散通道。

sentences.en: Exits and egress were a problem, people thought, for the tenements and the poor-quality buildings.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，出口和疏散是公寓楼和劣质建筑的问题。

sentences.en: The logic was, if a building was first class, it was in and of itself safe for the occupants.
sentences.zh: 当时的逻辑是，如果一栋建筑是一流的，那么它本身对里面的住户就是安全的。

sentences.en: And then the people could just be safely locked inside of these non-combustible buildings.
sentences.zh: 然后人们就可以安全地被锁在这些不可燃的建筑里面。

sentences.en: The Triangle Fire proved that architecture couldn't protect us.
sentences.zh: 三角火灾证明了建筑无法保护我们。

sentences.en: We had to protect ourselves from architecture.
sentences.zh: 我们必须保护自己免受建筑的伤害。

sentences.en: This is when an organization called the National Fire Protection Association does a lot of studies and thinking about egress.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，一个名为“国家消防协会”的组织对疏散进行了大量的研究和思考。

sentences.en: And good egress meant getting rid of fire escapes for so many reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于诸多原因，良好的疏散意味着摆脱防火梯。

sentences.en: They weren't commonly used, so they were often out of order or in states of disrepair.
sentences.zh: 它们不常被使用，因此经常失修或处于损坏状态。

sentences.en: In northern climates, they were covered with snow or eroded by rain.
sentences.zh: 在北方气候下，它们被积雪覆盖或被雨水侵蚀。

sentences.en: And not everyone could access them, like people with disabilities and the very young and the elderly and women who were hamstrung by the fashion of the time.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都能使用它们，比如残疾人、极年幼者、老人以及被当时时尚所束缚的女性。

sentences.en: Women in these long skirts might not have the presence of mind to take off their skirt, you know, so they could actually get out.
sentences.zh: 穿着这些长裙的女性可能没有清醒的头脑去脱掉裙子，你知道的，这样她们才能真正逃出去。

sentences.en: Also, fire escapes are scary.
sentences.zh: 此外，防火梯很吓人。

sentences.en: You see some narrow, rickety staircases on really tall buildings that make you feel like you should strap on rubber shoes and a parachute hat.
sentences.zh: 你在非常高的建筑上看到一些狭窄、摇晃的楼梯，会让你觉得应该绑上橡胶鞋和降落伞帽。

sentences.en: And if people weren't used to using fire escapes, they often didn't know where they were.
sentences.zh: 如果人们不习惯使用防火梯，他们通常不知道它们在哪里。

sentences.en: People try to leave the way they came in.
sentences.zh: 人们试图按原路返回离开。

sentences.en: You know, that's what they think of.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们就是这么想的。

sentences.en: And that's where modern fire escapes come in.
sentences.zh: 现代防火梯应运而生。

sentences.en: They're not bolted to the side of the building.
sentences.zh: 它们不是用螺栓固定在建筑侧面的。

sentences.en: They are the logical place where you would go in an emergency.
sentences.zh: 它们是你遇到紧急情况时合乎逻辑的去处。

sentences.en: They are the stairs.
sentences.zh: 它们就是楼梯。

sentences.en: Well, they look like normal stairs, but really, they're pieces of emergency equipment.
sentences.zh: 好吧，它们看起来像普通的楼梯，但实际上，它们是应急设备。

sentences.en: Enclosed in fireproof walls and sealed with a self-closing door and covered with sprinklers and alarMs.
sentences.zh: 封闭在防火墙内，用自动闭门器密封，并覆盖着喷淋系统和警报器。

sentences.en: And because they work perfectly well as stairways, they're often the stairway in a building.
sentences.zh: 而且因为它们作为楼梯运行得非常好，所以它们通常就是建筑中的楼梯。

sentences.en: So the building won't have the grand stairway any longer.
sentences.zh: 因此，建筑将不再拥有宏伟的楼梯。

sentences.en: It'll have lots of elevators and the fire stairs.
sentences.zh: 它会有很多电梯和消防楼梯。

sentences.en: Goodbye opulent lobbies with sweeping grand stairways.
sentences.zh: 告别带有宏伟宽大楼梯的豪华大堂吧。

sentences.en: If you like to take the stairs, you've probably already bemoaned the fact that they are always shoved off into a tower and are very cold and industrial,
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢走楼梯，你可能已经抱怨过这样一个事实：无论建筑从外面看起来如何，它们总是被塞进一个塔楼里，而且非常寒冷和工业化，

sentences.en: no matter what the building looks like from the outside.
sentences.zh: 无论建筑外观如何。

sentences.en: If we want, we can make them look good.
sentences.zh: 如果我们愿意，我们可以让它们看起来很不错。

sentences.en: But most clients elect to spend their money on things that people are going to see more.
sentences.zh: 但大多数客户选择把钱花在人们更能看到的地方。

sentences.en: Office mate and architect Adam Weinig again.
sentences.zh: 再次请出办公室同事兼建筑师亚当·韦尼格。

sentences.en: The stairways need to be what's called rated,
sentences.zh: 楼梯需要达到所谓的“耐火等级”，

sentences.en: meaning that they need to be enclosed in a type of construction that won't melt or allow the fire to penetrate as quickly as a non-rated wall.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们需要被包裹在一种不会熔化或让火势像非耐火墙那样迅速穿透的建筑结构中。

sentences.en: These rated towers can be like buildings within buildings.
sentences.zh: 这些有耐火等级的塔楼可以像建筑内的建筑一样。

sentences.en: The prime example of a souped-up fire stairway is in Freedom Tower.
sentences.zh: 升级版消防楼梯的典型例子就在自由塔中。

sentences.en: The Freedom Tower, which has this emergency core, which is on its own separate electrical and plumbing system and has its own elevator, its own stairs.
sentences.zh: 自由塔拥有这样一个应急核心筒，它拥有自己独立的电力和管道系统，并有自己的电梯、自己的楼梯。

sentences.en: That's Elijah Huge.
sentences.zh: 那是伊莱贾·休奇。

sentences.en: He's a professor at Wesleyan University.
sentences.zh: 他是卫斯理大学的教授。

sentences.en: And I'm also a practicing architect, and I run a small firm called Periphery Projects.
sentences.zh: 我也是一名执业建筑师，我经营着一家名为 Periphery Projects 的小型事务所。

sentences.en: And part of that periphery involves doing research on architecture and emergency.
sentences.zh: 这其中的外围工作包括对建筑和紧急情况进行研究。

sentences.en: He's particularly fascinated by these core structures around the fire stairs.
sentences.zh: 他对消防楼梯周围的核心筒结构特别着迷。

sentences.en: And these emergency cores are modeled with software and simulations dedicated solely to egress.
sentences.zh: 这些应急核心筒是通过专门用于疏散的软件和模拟来进行建模的。

sentences.en: This program, Exodus 4.0, I think there's now Exodus 5.0,
sentences.zh: 这个名为 Exodus 4.0 的程序，我想现在有 Exodus 5.0 了，

sentences.en: can simulate how quickly a floor of a building can be cleared based on the maximum number of bodies that would be allowed in the space.
sentences.zh: 可以根据空间中允许的最大人数来模拟清空一层建筑的速度有多快。

sentences.en: How quickly could those bodies exit the space?
sentences.zh: 这些人离开空间的速度能有多快？

sentences.en: So the architect, or actually more likely the consultant, will plug in the measurements of a building, all the information about its emergency equipment,
sentences.zh: 因此，建筑师，或者更可能是顾问，会输入建筑物的尺寸、有关其应急设备的所有信息、

sentences.en: the maximum number of occupants, and basically click play and watch the digital people escape the pixel flames.
sentences.zh: 最大占用人数，然后基本上点击播放，看着数字人在像素火焰中逃生。

sentences.en: A lot of agent-based modeling programs with humans don't work terribly well because humans don't necessarily behave predictably.
sentences.zh: 许多基于智能体的有人类参与的建模程序效果并不算太好，因为人类的行为不一定可预测。

sentences.en: But in emergencies, they do.
sentences.zh: 但在紧急情况下，他们会的。

sentences.en: Given adequate signage, people will behave in predictable ways in the event of an emergency.
sentences.zh: 如果有充足的标识，人们在紧急情况下会有可预测的行为。

sentences.en: So this makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这说得通。

sentences.en: We've already established that in an emergency, people don't want to go places they haven't gone to before, or use devices they've never seen, or, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们之前已经确定，在紧急情况下，人们不想去他们没去过的地方，不想使用他们没见过的设备，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: figure out if they can catch a rope shot at them with a bow and arrow.
sentences.zh: 去琢磨他们能不能接住用弓箭射过来的绳子。

sentences.en: The way egress works now is in keeping with the way that we use buildings normally.
sentences.zh: 现在的疏散方式与我们平时使用建筑物的方式是一致的。

sentences.en: Even though raided towers take up a lot of space and money, and make for an unpleasant stepping experience, it's hard to argue with this solution.
sentences.zh: 尽管突防塔占据了大量的空间和资金，踩上去的体验也不太愉快，但这个解决方案无可厚非。

sentences.en: It's paid off, let's say.
sentences.zh: 可以说，这是有回报的。

sentences.en: Sarah Wormiel again.
sentences.zh: 再次请到莎拉·沃米尔。

sentences.en: For 2012, in non-residential structures, there were 65 deaths in the whole year.
sentences.zh: 在2012年，非住宅建筑全年共有65人死亡。

sentences.en: You know, probably more people were struck by lightning.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，可能被闪电击中的人还更多。

sentences.en: Actually, 28 people were struck by lightning in 2012.
sentences.zh: 事实上，2012年有28人被闪电击中。

sentences.en: But still, even though each one is a tragedy, 65 deaths doesn't strike me as all that many.
sentences.zh: 但尽管每起事故都是一场悲剧，65人死亡在我看来并不算太多。

sentences.en: This number is already down from 2003, where there were 220 deaths in non-residential buildings.
sentences.zh: 这个数字已经比2003年有所下降，当年非住宅建筑有220人死亡。

sentences.en: So these are the buildings with heavy regulations and core structures.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是受到严格监管和拥有核心结构的建筑。

sentences.en: Modern emergency equipment and egress procedures are really helping to minimize the effects of fire accidents.
sentences.zh: 现代应急设备和疏散程序确实有助于将火灾事故的影响降到最低。

sentences.en: But from an aesthetic standpoint, it's almost a pity.
sentences.zh: 但从审美的角度来看，这几乎是一种遗憾。

sentences.en: Because fire escapes are beautiful.
sentences.zh: 因为太平梯非常美丽。

sentences.en: And although I'm not really thrilled at the prospect of clambering down the fire escape outside my window, I do like to look at it.
sentences.zh: 虽然我对爬窗外的太平梯这种前景实在提不起兴趣，但我确实喜欢看它。

sentences.en: And for Sarah Wormiel, fire escapes, even the ones that are no longer in use, are this physical reminder that we evolve past being a culture that says,
sentences.zh: 对莎拉·沃米尔来说，太平梯，甚至是那些不再使用的太平梯，是一个物理上的提醒，提醒我们已经不再是一个说着这种话的社会了：

sentences.en: Here's a rope.
sentences.zh: 给你一根绳子。

sentences.en: Good luck, buddy.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运，老兄。

sentences.en: I just like seeing them and hope that they'll be preserved.
sentences.zh: 我只是喜欢看到它们，并希望它们能被保存下来。

sentences.en: Because it just makes me realize how we kind of have to work together as a society.
sentences.zh: 因为这让我意识到，作为一个社会，我们必须如何共同努力。

sentences.en: You have to rely on other people to put in the stairs, to follow the rules, for the rules to be there.
sentences.zh: 你必须依靠其他人来安装楼梯、遵守规则、让规则存在。

sentences.en: And that's what makes us safe.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点保障了我们的安全。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Avery Truffleman, with Sam Greenspan, Katie Mingle, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由埃弗里·特鲁夫曼制作，萨姆·格林斯潘、凯蒂·明格和我——罗曼·马尔斯共同制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 Local Public Radio KALW in San Francisco, and produced out of the offices of ArcSign in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7地方公共广播电台KALW的一个项目，在加利福尼亚州美丽的奥克兰市中心ArcSign的办公室制作。

sentences.en: If you like the stories on this program, you can get more and more and more stories and correspond with all the people who make this show on Facebook, Twitter, and Tumblr.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个节目的故事，你可以在Facebook、Twitter和Tumblr上获取更多更多的故事，并与制作这个节目的所有人进行交流。

sentences.en: But there are more fire escapes than you can shake a stick at at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但在 99pi.org 上，有着数不清的太平梯供你探索。
